note.en: Neuter: "das Daily", "im Daily", "nach dem Daily". The long form "tägliches Stand-up-Meeting" is for job ads.

der-blocker.en: something that stops you from making progress

note.en: The plural has no ending: "keine Blocker".

durch-sein.en: to be done, to be through

note.en: "Das Ticket ist durch" means finished and off your plate. "Fertig" is correct too. "Durch" is what you hear.

haengen.en: to be stuck; in a call: to freeze

note.en: "Ich häng da" is about you and a problem. "Du hängst" is about your video or audio.

drueberschauen.en: to take a quick look over something

note.en: Short for "darüberschauen". It means a light check, not a full review.
In German offices it means "just the two of us, outside the meeting". No diplomacy involved.
Separable: "Ich setze das Projekt neu auf."
Separable: "Fahr mal den Server hoch." The opposite is "runterfahren".

feierabend.en: the end of the working day

note.en: "Schönen Feierabend!" is the standard goodbye when someone logs off for the day.
"halt" marks a fact that nobody is going to change. "eben" does the same job.
"quasi" says the label is close enough, not exact.

genau.en: Right. On to the next point, then.

note.en: "Genau" is agreement. Alone at the start of a sentence, it often just closes the topic.

mal.en: Have a quick look at it.

note.en: "mal" turns an order into a casual request. "kurz" promises it will not take long.
A check that you are still following. Often said with a slight rise, like "right?". Nobody expects an answer.
"an etwas dran sein" means to be working on something. Dropping "Ich" at the start is normal in speech.

fast-durch.de: Ist fast durch, muss nur noch getestet werden.
fast-durch.en: It's almost done, it just needs testing.

haeng-ich.de: Da häng ich grad ein bisschen.

note.en: "ein bisschen" is politeness. It can mean very stuck.

title.de: Ein Daily von Anfang bis Ende

lines.speaker: a
lines.en: Morning, everyone! Who wants to start?

lines.speaker: b
lines.de: Ich mach mal. Also, gestern hab ich noch am Login-Ticket gesessen.
lines.en: I'll go. So, yesterday I was still working on the login ticket.

lines.speaker: b
lines.de: Ist fast durch, muss halt nur noch getestet werden.
lines.en: It's almost done, it just needs testing.

lines.speaker: b
lines.de: Heute schau ich mir den Bug im Checkout an. Da häng ich grad ein bisschen.
lines.en: Today I'm looking at the checkout bug. I'm a bit stuck there.

lines.speaker: a
lines.de: Soll ich nach dem Daily mal kurz mit draufschauen?
lines.en: Should I take a quick look with you after the daily?

lines.speaker: b
lines.de: Ja, gerne. Lass uns das danach kurz bilateral klären.
lines.en: Yes, please. Let's sort it out between the two of us afterwards.

lines.speaker: b
lines.de: Sonst keine Blocker von meiner Seite. Das war's von mir.
lines.en: Otherwise, no blockers from my side. That's it from me.

question.en: What does "Ich bin da noch dran." mean?

explanation.en: "An etwas dran sein" means you are in the middle of it. Finished would be "Ist durch". "I'm next" would be "Ich bin dran", without "da noch".

question.en: What does "Lass uns das bilateral klären." mean?

text.en: Let's discuss it with the whole team.
Let's sort it out between the two of us.
Let's write it in two languages.

explanation.en: The two people involved take it out of the meeting. Everyone else gets their time back.

question.en: "Genau." at the start of a sentence in a call usually signals:

explanation.en: It sounds like agreement, and sometimes it is. At the start of a sentence in a call, it mostly closes one topic and opens the next.
